name: SWE-Exp: Experience-Driven Software Issue Resolution
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2507.23361, cs.SE); submitted 31 Jul 2025, revised 2 Feb 2026. No peer-reviewed venue confirmed as of this survey.
authors_affiliation: Silin Chen, Yuling Shi, Xiaodong Gu (corresponding) (Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Shaoxin Lin, Dong Chen, Lin Cao, Jiyang Liu, Nu Xia, Qianxiang Wang (Huawei); Heng Lian (Xidian University); Longfei Yun (UC San Diego).
code_url: https://github.com/cslsolow/SWE-Exp (linked in paper as https://github.com/YerbaPage/SWE-Exp, redirects to cslsolow/SWE-Exp); anonymous replication: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SWE-Exp-6FEA
task_domain: code (repository-level / GitHub software issue resolution; automated program repair by LLM agents).
problem_setting: Interactive, multi-step repository-level issue resolution on SWE-Bench-Verified: the agent reads a natural-language issue, navigates the codebase, localizes faults, and generates a patch verified by test execution. Supervision is available offline (ground-truth golden patches used to annotate success/failure trajectories during experience collection). It is multi-agent (dual-agent Instructor/Assistant on top of MCTS / SWE-Search) with a growing cross-repository experience bank built before test-time. Cross-issue continual learning is the core goal: knowledge distilled from prior agent trajectories is reused across different issues and repositories. Data-leakage controls exclude same-repository and temporally-posterior experiences.
what_is_retrieved: Distilled, reusable 'experiences' mined from prior agent repair trajectories. Two facets: Comprehension experiences (perspective: abstract understanding/diagnostic reasoning patterns for the problem) and Modification experiences (generalized code-modification strategies/safety patterns). Both successful and failed trajectories are distilled; failed ones yield reflections/corrective insights.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes (the Experience Bank), induced offline from past agent trajectories rather than a static external corpus of docs/APIs. The bank is constructed before test-time on SWE-Bench-Verified trajectories; it is not updated during a single online resolution.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Precision-driven, very small selection. Phase 1 retrieves a fixed top-N=10 candidates by error-type/description similarity; an LLM rerank agent then selects k=1 most-applicable experience. The paper finds 1 experience is optimal (more degrades performance), so the objective is precision/quality over completeness or large top-k recall.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve: yes (similarity + LLM rerank). Reuse: yes (LLM adapts/generalizes retrieved experience to current issue and rewrites instructions). Revise: partial (experiences are contextualized/adapted per-issue at reuse time). Retain: yes offline (trajectories distilled into the experience bank), but not online during test-time. Flags: [Retrieve=yes, Reuse=yes, Revise=partial, Retain=offline-only].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as 'experience-driven' / 'experience-enhanced' continual learning and memory-augmented agents; it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or use case-based reasoning terminology, though it realizes CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Adapt mechanisms.
retrieval_unit: Distilled experience entry = a (perspective, modification) dictionary derived from a past trajectory, indexed by metadata (issue_type, description). Effectively a distilled case/guideline pair rather than a raw trajectory; comprehension experiences are diagnostic insights, modification experiences are repair-strategy rules.
index_source: Growing memory built offline / before test-time: trajectories are collected by running SWE-Search on SWE-Bench-Verified, then distilled into experiences stored in a vector database (the Experience Bank). Frozen during a given online resolution run (no per-instance write-back at inference).
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index (vector database) with metadata keying. Each experience is embedded and indexed by two metadata attributes (issue_type label and a generalized description); also organized into two facet categories (comprehension vs modification).
retriever_type: Hybrid two-stage: (1) dense embedding similarity (Multilingual-E5-Large-Instruct, cosine similarity) over issue_type+description, then (2) LLM-as-reranker (a rerank/select agent picks the most applicable experience).
retriever_learning_signal: None for the embedding retriever (off-the-shelf pre-trained Multilingual-E5-Large-Instruct, no fine-tuning). Final selection is LLM-judgment-based (prompted reranking agent), not a trained policy; no contrastive or RL training of the retriever is reported.
query_construction: Query is the new issue's extracted issue_type label plus a generalized description (an issue agent classifies the problem statement into an error type and description). For reuse, the agent compares the current problem_statement and code-exploration history with retrieved past issue descriptions/experiences and rewrites/adapts them.
query_granularity: Two-level. Task-level: issue_type/description query for the initial similarity retrieval. Step/decision-level: experiences are also retrieved/integrated at critical MCTS decision nodes during tree expansion (per-decision contextual guidance).
when_to_retrieve: Iterative within the MCTS search: relevant experiences are dynamically retrieved at critical decision points during tree expansion, not just one-shot at t=0. Retrieval is on a fixed schedule tied to decision nodes (not uncertainty-triggered or learned-router).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule tied to MCTS decision points: before each decision / at decision nodes during tree expansion the agent retrieves the N most relevant experiences. No token-confidence, attention, or learned-complexity trigger; integration is keyed to the search-tree expansion steps.
reranking: Yes. A dedicated LLM rerank agent (RerankAgent / select agent) takes the top N=10 similarity candidates and selects k=1 most-applicable experience. Ablation shows replacing LLM reranking with plain similarity selection drops Pass@1 from 42.0% to 38.2% (-3.8%).
retrieved_context_refinement: Adapt/generalize-then-inject. The reuse agent contextualizes the retrieved experience to the current issue (compares similarities/differences, produces a 'new_experience' tailored to the current problem) and rewrites the Assistant's next-step instruction ('enhanced_instruction') using modification experience. Comprehension experience is added as message context rather than forcibly cited (to avoid over-reliance).
tool_document_engineering: N/A (this work retrieves distilled experiences/cases, not tools or tool/API documents).
index_content_separation: Partial: experiences are indexed by lightweight metadata keys (issue_type + short description) embedded for similarity search, while the fuller perspective/modification content is the retrieved payload used downstream; not framed as a progressive-disclosure SOP-index-then-content design.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no live tool index or external tool integration protocol; integration is with the SWE-Search/moatless MCTS framework and a vector DB).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling; retrieval is over experiences, not tools).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation + case adaptation. Retrieved comprehension experience is injected into the Instructor's context to guide high-level diagnosis/strategy; retrieved modification experience is used to rewrite/enhance the Assistant's next-step instruction. No model fine-tuning; experience is used in-context to steer MCTS action selection and value assessment.
planning_integration: Inside MCTS / tree search. Built on SWE-Search MCTS: experiences are retrieved at decision nodes and integrated into the Selection, Expansion, Evaluation, and Discrimination stages (experience-guided node selection, experience-informed action generation, experience-enhanced value assessment, experience-informed consensus). A hierarchical dual-agent (Instructor planner + Assistant executor) maps experiences to strategic planning vs tactical execution across the three-stage workflow (Issue Understanding, Fault Localization, Patch Generation).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-decision-step within an MCTS rollout: experiences are woven in at decision nodes / per next-step instruction (Instructor decides a strategic action, Assistant's instruction is experience-enhanced), i.e. finer than per-answer; effectively per MCTS action/instruction.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation: a Reuser agent generalizes the retrieved past experience into a 'new_experience' tailored to the current problem statement and rewrites the next-step instruction ('enhanced_instruction'). Comprehension experience is provided as soft message context (not forced) to avoid inflexible over-reliance; no RL-reuse-finetuning.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled strategy/guideline in free text: comprehension experiences are natural-language diagnostic insights/perspectives; modification experiences are natural-language repair-strategy rules. Stored structurally as a (perspective, modification[]) dictionary with issue_type/description metadata. Not raw trajectories and not executable programs.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled strategy/insight and state-aware guideline/rule: high-level problem-comprehension perspectives plus generalized code-modification strategies abstracted across repositories. Explicitly multi-level (from high-level problem comprehension to specific code-change strategies), but abstracted rather than raw trajectories.
noise_robustness_mechanism: (1) LLM reranking to filter to the single most-relevant experience; (2) empirically capping k=1 (more experiences introduce conflicting/misleading info and degrade performance); (3) providing comprehension experience as non-forced message context to prevent over-reliance; (4) facet separation so modification experience is vetted by the Assistant against the Instructor's decided direction; (5) data-leakage exclusion (same-repo and temporally-posterior experiences removed). No retriever-aware training or distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: episodic / experience bank (distilled-experience memory) realized as a vector database; organized into two facet categories (comprehension, modification). Not a skill-library of executable skills, not a graph.
write_back: True (offline). The system distills new experiences from collected success and failure trajectories and stores them in the Experience Bank vector DB. However, this happens in the offline extraction stage, not as online write-back during a single test-time resolution run.
online_growth: No (as evaluated). The Experience Bank is induced offline before test-time and frozen during online resolution; the paper does not perform per-instance write-back at inference. The RQ3 'experience bank size' study grows the bank in chronological increments (offline simulation of growth), not live streaming growth during deployment.
write_back_trigger: On-success-and-failure (offline): both successful trajectories (correct patches validated against ground truth) and failed trajectories are distilled into experiences; failure trajectories get additional failure-cause metadata (incorrect localization / flawed modification strategy / insufficient comprehension). Triggered by the offline extraction pipeline using ground-truth validation, not by online self-critique at test time.
failure_experience_usage: Success + failure. Failure trajectories are explicitly distilled into corrective 'reflections' insights and annotated with failure cause; the bank captures both successful repair patterns and failed-attempt lessons. For success extraction the shortest path is used; for failure the longest. Comprehension reuse can draw on either a success perspective or failure reflections.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only (entries are distilled once and stored; the paper does not describe mutating/merging/forgetting stored entries after writing). Adaptation happens at reuse time on a copy (generated new_experience), not by overwriting bank entries.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval is fixed similarity top-N=10 plus an LLM-prompted reranking agent selecting k=1; it is not an RL-/value-trained selection policy (no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, or learned retrieval policy).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Cross-issue and cross-repository experience sharing within a single agent framework: experiences distilled from heterogeneous external repositories are aggregated and reused across issues/repositories (a key differentiator vs SAGE's within-instance experience). It is not framed as sharing across heterogeneous agent frameworks or multiple distinct agents; the Instructor/Assistant share one experience bank.
benchmarks: SWE-Bench-Verified (500 human-verified issues from SWE-bench). Hyperparameter studies use a 75-instance subset (25 each from Django, SymPy, Sphinx).
baselines: Agentless; SWE-Agent; SWE-Search (MCTS; the framework SWE-Exp extends); OpenHands; EvoCoder (experience-driven continual learning); SAGE (experience/plan-abstraction framework on OpenHands). Models: DeepSeek-V3-0324 (open-source) and Claude-4-Sonnet (20250514, closed-source).
key_metrics: Pass@1 resolution rate (proportion of issues correctly fixed on first attempt). Cost metrics: average token cost, average API cost (USD), average wall-clock time, average retrieval+rerank time.
headline_result: 73.0% Pass@1 on SWE-Bench-Verified with Claude-4-Sonnet (vs SWE-Search 70.8%, SAGE 71.6%, OpenHands 70.4%, EvoCoder 67.8%, Agentless 66.6% on the same model). With DeepSeek-V3-0324: 42.0% Pass@1 (vs SWE-Search 35.4%, OpenHands/SWE-Agent/EvoCoder 38.8%/38.8%/38.0%, Agentless 36.6%).
ablations: On DeepSeek-V3-0324 (base SWE-Exp 42.0%): w/o Comprehension Experience 38.8% (-3.2%); w/o Modification Experience 39.4% (-2.6%); w/o Dual-Agent 39.8% (-2.2%); w/o Experiences Extraction (use raw problem statement + golden patch as in-context demos) 36.0% (-6.0%, largest drop); w/o LLM Reranking (plain similarity selection) 38.2% (-3.8%). RQ3 hyperparameters: number of experiences peaks at 1 (42.0%; 0 experiences = 37.8%/37.2%, declines to 39.8% at 2 and ~39.0% at 4); experience-bank size shows steady gains up to ~300 experiences then saturation.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (Pass@1) and cost metrics are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / experience-retrieval accuracy) are reported separately.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (Pass@1). Process is examined qualitatively via a case study (django-11964) and a manual quality verification of extracted experiences on 75 instances, plus cost/runtime; no quantitative step-wise retrieval/planning-accuracy or trajectory-quality metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Modest overhead vs SWE-Search (DeepSeek-V3-0324): avg token cost 203.3K vs 189.1K; avg API cost $0.13 vs $0.12; avg wall time 15min49s vs 12min37s; experience retrieval+rerank adds ~37.5s/instance (0s for SWE-Search). Authors conclude large accuracy gains come at minimal extra compute/cost.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Reranked-then-truncated to a very small k: N=10 similarity candidates reranked by an LLM agent down to k=1 experience injected per instance. Empirically k=1 is optimal; larger k degrades performance. No explicit token budget cap reported for injected experiences.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing SWE-Bench-Verified, not a newly constructed benchmark; 500 human-verified issues, human-curated ground-truth patches, test-execution-verifiable).
builds_on: SWE-Search (Antoniades et al., 2024) MCTS framework / moatless-tree-search (Albert Orwall) as the base; SWE-bench / SWE-Bench-Verified (Jimenez et al., 2024; OpenAI 2024) as the testbed; experience-enhanced agent line such as ExpeL (experiential learners), AutoGuide (context-aware guidelines), ExACT (Reflective-MCTS + vector DB), EvoCoder, SAGE.
contrasts_with: Memoryless / single-instance agents: SWE-Agent, OpenHands, Agentless (no cross-issue experience reuse); SWE-Search (MCTS without experience). Among experience-driven methods, contrasts with SAGE (within-instance plan abstraction, experience localized to current instance) and EvoCoder (reproduction-focused continual learning), arguing SWE-Exp uniquely abstracts and reuses experience across trajectories from different repositories with a multi-facet (comprehension+modification) bank and dual-agent reuse.
lineage: Group E (tool-use / agentic) — experience/memory-augmented coding agents: extends the MCTS-based SWE issue-resolution line (SWE-Search) with a growing, distilled cross-repository experience bank, positioned in the experiential-learning lineage (ExpeL -> AutoGuide -> ExACT / EvoCoder / SAGE -> SWE-Exp), specialized for repository-level software issue resolution.
